solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Not the principal allegiance temp is bound by at intervals (6)

indicators.note: the letters from 'temp' sit tied up inside the word for allegiance
take every other letter of 'temp'

blocks.note: duty is what you owe, your allegiance
second and fourth letters of TEMP

annotation.surface: An office temp is caught between loyalty to the boss and to someone less senior.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Temp' looks like the deputy itself, but it only supplies two letters; 'Not the principal' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A deputy acts for someone else and is not the principal.

entries.clue: Make little of not working on stage show (8)

blocks.note: a system that is down is not working
a play is a show on stage

annotation.surface: Someone belittles a stage show that has stopped running.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts DOWN above PLAY.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to play something down is to minimise its importance.

entries.clue: Each year, worry about relating to faithless people (5)

indicators.note: the word for worry is turned about

blocks.note: per annum, abbreviated PA
to nag is to worry at someone

annotation.surface: Every year someone frets over people who have lost their faith.
annotation.walkthrough: PA is 'per annum', Latin for each year.
annotation.definitionFit: Pagan describes those outside the main faiths, seen as faithless.

entries.clue: Secure draw (3)

blocks.note: a verb: fasten with a knot
a noun: a match with no winner

annotation.surface: A team makes sure of a draw.
annotation.walkthrough: Both words are read as verbs in the surface; 'draw' is the noun, a tied result.
annotation.definitionFit: You tie a knot to secure it, and a match that ends level is a tie.

entries.clue: No striking poet, but there may be some steel here (8)

definitions.text: there may be some steel here

blocks.note: a scab is a worker who will not join a strike
a bard is a poet

annotation.surface: A poet refuses to join a strike, yet he has some steel in him.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Steel' suggests backbone; here it is a sword, which sits in a scabbard.
annotation.definitionFit: A scabbard is the sheath that holds a steel blade.

entries.clue: Start of career not so rich for office worker (7)

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: first letter of CAREER
lean food is less rich

annotation.surface: Someone begins working life on poorer wages in an office.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Office worker' suggests a clerk; it is the person who cleans the office.
annotation.definitionFit: Office cleaners work in offices after hours.

entries.clue: Initiate pupils in vital course (11)

blocks.note: to blood a newcomer is to initiate them
a stream is a group of pupils of similar ability

annotation.surface: Pupils are introduced to an essential school course.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Course' reads as a school subject; here it is the course the blood flows, which is vital to life. In British schools pupils are grouped by ability into streams.
annotation.definitionFit: The bloodstream is the flowing course of blood, vital to life.

entries.clue: Opponent of government is tense after seconds of fairly unpleasant teasing (9)

indicators.note: take the second letter of each word
IS T is placed after the other pieces

blocks.note: second letters of FAIRLY and UNPLEASANT
arch means playfully teasing
used as it stands
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

annotation.surface: A rebel grows tense after a round of mildly nasty mockery.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Teasing' is not part of the letter selection; it gives ARCH as a whole word.
annotation.definitionFit: Anarchy means rule by no one, so its supporter is against any government at all.

entries.clue: Make out drama’s opening key lines (6)

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: first letter of DRAMA
the Escape key on a keyboard
RY is short for railway, a set of lines

annotation.surface: An actor works out the key lines at the start of a play.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Key' and 'lines' look like theatre words; one is a computer key, the other a railway.
annotation.definitionFit: A literary synonym: to catch sight of something far off, as in making out a ship on the horizon.

entries.clue: Ground seeds popular among staff (6)

indicators.note: IN goes among the letters of the staff

blocks.note: a pole is a staff
in means fashionable, popular

annotation.surface: Some seeds have become fashionable with the employees.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Staff' suggests employees; it is a wooden pole.
annotation.definitionFit: Pinole is a flour of ground seeds or grains, from Mexico and the American Southwest.

entries.clue: Lover of composer’s wit, broadcast entire (9)

indicators.note: the letters of ENTIRE are scattered like seed

blocks.note: a wag is a wit, a joker
ENTIRE rearranged

annotation.surface: A music lover repeats a composer's joke in full on air.
annotation.walkthrough: The ’s means 'has': the lover of the composer has WAG plus the rearrangement.
annotation.definitionFit: A Wagnerite is an enthusiast for Wagner's music.

entries.clue: Medical procedure in addition cut stones (5)

indicators.note: the word for 'in addition' loses its last letter

blocks.note: an op is a surgical operation
ALSO without its last letter

annotation.surface: A surgeon also removes kidney stones.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cut stones' sounds like gems or gallstones being cut; 'cut' works on ALSO.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the opal is one kind of gemstone, prized for its shifting colours.

entries.clue: God with hooked fingers catches nothing in trousers (11)

indicators.note: the word for hooked fingers catches O inside it

blocks.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild
talons are hooked claws
O looks like zero

annotation.surface: A clawed god grabs nothing in his trousers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In trousers' looks like where the nothing is caught; it is the definition, an adjective for someone wearing them.
annotation.definitionFit: Pantaloons are trousers, so pantalooned means wearing them.

entries.clue: Turn up with cider unexpectedly: cheers! (11)

indicators.note: the letters of CIDER come out in an unexpected order

blocks.note: to turn up is to arrive
CIDER rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone surprises the party by arriving with cider and raising a toast.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cheers!' reads as a toast; it is the British informal goodbye.
annotation.definitionFit: Arrivederci is Italian for goodbye, as 'cheers' is in British speech.

entries.clue: I’m surprised fabulous bird has come from the east (3)

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming from the east means read right to left

blocks.note: the roc is a giant bird of fable

annotation.surface: Someone is amazed that a mythical bird has flown in from the Orient.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' means from fable, not wonderful.
annotation.definitionFit: Cor! is a British exclamation of surprise.

entries.clue: Almost lost moisture out of doors in Scots town (7)

indicators.note: the word is not quite complete: drop its last letter

blocks.note: in the open air is out of doors
DRIED without its last letter

annotation.surface: Washing hung outside nearly dried in a Scottish town.
annotation.walkthrough: The pieces appear in reverse order to the clue: AIR comes first.
annotation.definitionFit: Airdrie is a town east of Glasgow in North Lanarkshire.

entries.clue: Given inferior position on stage, very much resented losing top place (9)

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of the word is its first letter, which goes

blocks.note: re means on, concerning
a leg is a stage of a journey

blocks.clueFragment: very much resented losing top place
blocks.note: HATED without its first letter

annotation.surface: An actor pushed to the back of the stage bitterly resented being demoted from the lead.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On stage' looks like theatre, but the two words are separate pieces, and a stage here is part of a journey. Relegation is what happens to a British football team that drops a division.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, used of teams demoted to a lower league and of people pushed to lesser jobs.

entries.clue: Shop’s business turning round after receiving international investment (6)

indicators.note: the finished word is turned back to front
the word for after takes I in

blocks.note: later means after
I for international, invested inside

annotation.surface: A store's trade picks up after foreign investment arrives.
annotation.walkthrough: I goes in after the L of LATER to make LIATER, which is then read backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: Retail, selling to the public, is what a shop does.

entries.clue: Disguising my age, end as top-rank waiter? (8)

indicators.note: the letters are rearranged beyond recognition

blocks.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

annotation.surface: An ageing waiter hides how old he is to see out his career at the top.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Top-rank' is Olympus: Ganymede served wine to the gods, the highest company there is.
annotation.definitionFit: Ganymede was the cupbearer of the Greek gods.

entries.clue: Working at last, really enjoyed having something on hand (6)

indicators.note: take the last letter of 'working'

blocks.note: last letter of WORKING
to love something is to really enjoy it

annotation.surface: Someone finally back at work loves having a task ready to hand.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On hand' means available; here it is literal, something worn on the hand.
annotation.definitionFit: Gloved means wearing a glove, something on the hand.

entries.clue: County lass has finished on top (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue DONE sits above GAL

blocks.note: done means finished
gal is an informal word for a girl

annotation.surface: A country girl has come out on top.
annotation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads backwards: the lass is below, 'finished' is on top.
annotation.definitionFit: Donegal is a county in the north-west of Ireland.

entries.clue: Disinclination to move at home: it’s about dividing time (7)

indicators.note: to turn about is to face the other way, so the two letters swap round
the reversed pair splits the word for time into two parts

blocks.note: to be in is to be at home
an era is a period of time
used as it stands; the ’s that follows means 'is'

annotation.surface: Someone stays put at home, as time is split by it.
annotation.walkthrough: The ’s is 'is', joining the pieces: 'it is about, dividing time'.
annotation.definitionFit: Borrowed from physics, where a body at rest resists being moved; in people it is sluggish unwillingness to act.

entries.clue: Animals I live with upset relations (6)

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down

blocks.note: used as it stands
to be is to live, exist
sexual relations

annotation.surface: Someone lives with animals and has fallen out with the family.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Relations' suggests relatives, but it is sex.
annotation.definitionFit: Ibexes are wild mountain goats.

entries.clue: Like my phone? Old, black, not compact (6)

blocks.note: O is short for old
B for black, as on pencils
long is not compact

annotation.surface: Someone describes a phone as old, black and bulky.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: most phones are oblong.
annotation.definitionFit: A phone is a rectangle longer than it is wide.

entries.clue: Slough left out of journal (3)

indicators.note: L, for left, is taken out of the word

blocks.note: a blog is an online journal
L is short for left

annotation.surface: A word for marsh is missing from a diary.
annotation.walkthrough: Slough, rhyming with 'cow', is a swamp, not the Berkshire town.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both are soft, waterlogged ground, as in Bunyan's Slough of Despond.

entries.clue: Extra pay from slaughtering enemy dragon? (6,5)

indicators.note: the words are hacked apart and reassembled

blocks.note: the eleven letters to be rearranged

annotation.surface: A knight claims a bonus for killing a hostile dragon.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark signals that dragon-slaying is just the sort of job that earns it.
annotation.definitionFit: A British term for the bonus paid on top of wages for hazardous work.

entries.clue: Innocent individual’s first to occupy space for congregation (5)

indicators.note: take the first letter of 'individual'
the I moves into the word for the space

blocks.note: the nave is the main body of a church, where the congregation sits
first letter of INDIVIDUAL

annotation.surface: An innocent person is the first to take a seat in church.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Space for congregation' could be any hall; the church sense is the one wanted.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone naive is artless and unworldly, as an innocent is.

entries.clue: Swimmer got terrible cramps (5)

indicators.note: the words cramp, confine, the answer within them

blocks.note: gOT TERrible

annotation.surface: A swimmer suffered bad cramps.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cramps' reads as a noun; it is the verb, to confine.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the otter spends much of its life swimming in rivers and the sea.

entries.clue: Syrup dispersed anger, peace finally after row (9)

indicators.note: the letters of ANGER are scattered
take the last letter of 'peace'
after means following, so the letter from 'peace' is placed behind the word for row

blocks.note: ANGER rearranged
a din is a loud row
last letter of PEACE

annotation.surface: Something sweet calmed the anger and brought peace after a quarrel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Row' is a noisy quarrel, rhyming with 'cow', not a line.
annotation.definitionFit: Grenadine is a sweet red syrup flavoured with pomegranate.

entries.clue: Each and everybody (3)

blocks.note: the sense used in level scores, such as 'three apiece'
every person together

annotation.surface: Every single person.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Each' fits ALL only in scores: 'three all' is three each.
annotation.definitionFit: All means everybody, and in scoring it means each.

entries.clue: We hear Olympians, one and all, backed huge film star (8)

indicators.note: the Olympians are said, not spelt
the letters of 'all' are turned back

blocks.note: the Olympians are the Greek gods
I is the Roman numeral one
used as it stands

annotation.surface: The athletes backed a big movie star.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Olympians' suggests athletes; they are the gods on Mount Olympus.
annotation.definitionFit: Godzilla is the giant monster who stars in Japanese films.

entries.clue: Hurry away from church in warm coat (6)

blocks.note: to flee is to hurry away
CE is the Church of England

annotation.surface: Someone rushes out of church in a thick coat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hurry away from church' reads as one action, but it splits into two pieces; CE is the Church of England.
annotation.definitionFit: A fleece is a warm jacket of fleecy fabric, or a sheep's coat.
